title: Tensor-product Mittag-Leffler condition gives Mittag-Leffler Hom systems
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, and $(M_i,f_{ij})_{i\in I}$ a directed system of finitely presented $R$-modules. A module is finitely presented here if it is the cokernel of an $R$-linear map $R^a\to R^b$ for finite integers $a,b\ge0$. Let the compatible maps $M_i\to M$ exhibit an $R$-module $M$ as its colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose $M$ is Mittag-Leffler in the tensor-product sense [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module]. Then for every $R$-module $N$ and every $i\in I$ there is $j\ge i$ such that for every $k\ge j$ the images of the precomposition maps $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_k,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,N)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_j,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,N)$ are equal. No countability of $I$ or finite-generation assumption on $N$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), (2) implies (1), followed by Tag 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), condition (4).

proof.text: Fix $i\in I$ and write $u_s:M_s\to M$ for the given colimit maps. Form the set $B=\coprod_{a,b\ge0}\operatorname{Mat}_{b\times a}(R)$ and, for $t\in\operatorname{Mat}_{b\times a}(R)$, put $Q_t=R^b/\operatorname{im}(t)$. Every $Q_t$ is finitely presented and every finitely presented $R$-module is isomorphic to some $Q_t$, directly from its finite presentation [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Consequently $A=\{(t,z):t\in B,\ z\in\ker(u_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_{Q_t})\}$ is a set. For $\alpha=(t,z)$ put $Q_\alpha=Q_t$ and $z_\alpha=z$, and let $T=\prod_{\alpha\in A}Q_\alpha$, the module of all families. This explicitly supplies the set of test modules used by the source; no product over a proper class is taken.

source.place: Tag 059M, proposition-ML-tensor, proof of (2) implies (1), choice of the set B and pairs (Q,x).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-presentation-tensor-products] to $M_i$ and the family $(Q_\alpha)$ to obtain $z\in M_i\otimes_RT$ whose image under the canonical comparison is $(z_\alpha)_\alpha$. Put $y=(u_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_T)(z)$. Its image under $\theta_{M,(Q_\alpha)}$ is zero: the $\alpha$-coordinate is $(u_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_{Q_\alpha})(z_\alpha)=0$. The comparison square commutes because on a pure tensor $m\otimes(q_\alpha)_\alpha$ both composites have $\alpha$-coordinate $u_i(m)\otimes q_\alpha$; pure tensors generate [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The tensor-product Mittag-Leffler hypothesis [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module] makes $\theta_{M,(Q_\alpha)}$ injective. Thus $y=0$.

source.place: Tag 059M, proposition-ML-tensor, proof of (2) implies (1), the first commutative square and the kernel element x.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-commutes-with-colimits], the maps $u_s\otimes\mathrm{id}_T$ exhibit $M\otimes_RT$ as the colimit of $M_s\otimes_RT$. Since the image of $z$ is zero, [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] gives $j\ge i$ with $(f_{ij}\otimes\mathrm{id}_T)(z)=0$. Project to each $Q_\alpha$. The resulting equality is $(f_{ij}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{Q_\alpha})(z_\alpha)=0$, by the same pure-tensor calculation as in step 2 [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. In particular, for every $t\in B$ and every $v\in\ker(u_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_{Q_t})$, the coordinate $\alpha=(t,v)$ gives $(f_{ij}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{Q_t})(v)=0$. For any finitely presented $Q$, choose an isomorphism $e:Q\to Q_t$. The maps $1\otimes e$ and $1\otimes e^{-1}$ are inverse and intertwine all these maps: on $m\otimes q$ the commutation identity sends it to $f(m)\otimes e(q)$. Applying this identity and then the inverse transfers the kernel inclusion to $Q$. Therefore, for every finitely presented $Q$, $\ker(u_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)\subseteq\ker(f_{ij}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)$. The single index $j$ works for all these $Q$.

source.place: Tag 059M, proposition-ML-tensor, proof of (2) implies (1), killing the universal kernel element; use the given finitely presented directed system directly, as in Tag 059L, lemma-kernel-tensored-fp.

proof.text: Fix $k\ge j$. Since $u_i=u_k\circ f_{ik}$, functoriality of tensor [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and step 3 give $\ker(f_{ik}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)\subseteq\ker(f_{ij}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)$ for every finitely presented $Q$. The cokernel of $f_{ik}$ is finitely presented, as the following finite presentation shows. Choose generators $p_1,\ldots,p_c$ of $M_i$ and a presentation $M_k=R^b/\operatorname{im}(D)$ with $D:R^a\to R^b$, with all integers finite [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Choose lifts $v_r\in R^b$ of $f_{ik}(p_r)$. Then $M_k/f_{ik}(M_i)$ is the quotient of $R^b$ by $\operatorname{im}(D)+\sum_{r=1}^cRv_r$, hence is the cokernel of the finite matrix $(D\ v_1\ \cdots\ v_c):R^{a+c}\to R^b$. Indeed an element of $R^b$ maps to zero in this quotient exactly when its image in $M_k$ is a linear combination of the $f_{ik}(p_r)$, which is exactly membership in that displayed submodule.

source.place: Tag 059E, proposition-ML-characterization, proof of (2) implies (3), transitivity of domination and finite presentation of the transition cokernel.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-tensor-kernel-factorization] with $U=M_i$, $V=M_k$, $W=M_j$, $f=f_{ik}$ and $g=f_{ij}$. Both required hypotheses were verified in step 4: the cokernel of $f_{ik}$ is finitely presented and every finitely presented tensor test gives the stated kernel inclusion. Obtain an $R$-linear $h_k:M_k\to M_j$ with $f_{ij}=h_k\circ f_{ik}$. This applies to every $k\ge j$, with the same $j$ chosen in step 3.

source.place: Tag 059E, proposition-ML-characterization, proof of (2) implies (3), application of Tag 059D.

proof.text: Let $N$ be any $R$-module and $k\ge j$. An element of the image of $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_j,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,N)$ has the form $a\circ f_{ij}$ for $a:M_j\to N$. Step 5 rewrites it as $(a\circ h_k)\circ f_{ik}$, so it is in the image from $M_k$. Conversely, if $b:M_k\to N$, then $b\circ f_{ik}=(b\circ f_{jk})\circ f_{ij}$ by the directed-system identity $f_{ik}=f_{jk}\circ f_{ij}$. Thus the two images are equal for every $k\ge j$. This proves the required assertion for all $i$ and $N$, without countability or any finiteness condition on $N$.

source.place: Tag 059E, proposition-ML-characterization, (3) implies (4); both image inclusions written explicitly.

proof_origin.place: Tag 059M, proposition-ML-tensor, (2) implies (1), and Tag 059E, proposition-ML-characterization, (2) implies (3) implies (4). The universal kernel element is killed in the given system directly, as in Tag 059L.
